name: Last Will and Testament of Nobody in Particular
author: Unsigned; found folded inside a standard C-tier go-bag
description: A handwritten last will and testament recovered from a standard-issue C-tier go-bag found in a locker at the Shelf 7 gear exchange on the Narrows border, unclaimed for eleven months. The document was folded three times and sealed with a strip of packing tape that had been reused at least once. No date. No surname. Whoever left it either didn't come back for it or didn't need it. Submitted to the Signal Network archive by the locker operator, who said, and this is the full note she attached: 'somebody should have this.'
body:
LAST WILL AND TESTAMENT OF NOBODY IN PARTICULAR

Okay. I'm writing this before the Kowalczyk job because Demi told me to and also because I think Demi is right even though I hate that. This is not me being dramatic. This is me trying to be organized. If you are reading this and I didn't make it back, please try to do the things I'm asking. If you're reading this and I DID make it back then please don't tell anyone I wrote it because I will be embarrassed.

---

THE GEAR

The Keppler-Stross monofilament rig goes to Demi. She knows how to use it and she helped me buy it when I was short and she never asked me to pay her back but I have been tracking it and I owe her Φ340 on that, which I am noting here so whoever settles this can knock it off what I owe her total (see the DEBTS section). If the rig is damaged when I die you can probably sell the spool assembly at Carver's on Level 4, he'll give you maybe Φ60 for it, don't take less than Φ50.

The Brekka-9 goes to Tomás. I know he has two already but he loves that gun and I promised him a long time ago and I'm keeping the promise. It has a modification on the grip that I did myself with heat-set polymer and it's ugly but it works for my hand size and he can strip it off if he wants. There's a small scratch on the barrel from the Millhaven thing. He knows about the scratch.

The Faraday pouches (I have four, they're in the green bag inside the go-bag) can go to whoever needs them. They're not worth much but they work. Don't let Rocha take all of them. He already has too many Faraday pouches and he doesn't use half of them.

The medkit is stocked except for the coagulant foam which I used last month and didn't replace yet, I'm sorry, I know that's bad. What's left is still useful. Give it to Lena if she's still running. If she moved on, give it to the drop at the Shelf 9 intake clinic, they'll use it.

Boots: Demi again if her feet are close to mine (she can check). Otherwise sell them. They are good boots. I paid Φ180 for them and cried about it and then wore them every day for eight months so I think it evens out.

The rest of the clothes are honestly not worth distributing, just take whatever is useful and burn or donate the rest. There's a red jacket in the locker with the yellow stitching on the collar. That one I want kept. Don't give it away. If there's no one who wants to keep it for sentimental reasons then I want it put in the pile at the Level 2 exchange. A kid will want it. It should be a kid who wants something bright.

---

DEBTS (what I owe)

Φ340 to Demi — rig money, deducted if she takes the rig, zeroed if she takes the rig.
Φ80 to the woman at stall 14 in the Shelf 8 market, she sells noodles and I have a running tab and I know that's embarrassing but she always let me eat when I was short and I want her to get paid. Her name is Mrs. Pacheco or that's what everyone calls her. Find her, pay her.
Φ20 to Rocha for the tarp. I didn't ruin the tarp, I just never gave it back. He can have the tarp back instead of the money if it's easier.

DEBTS (what's owed to me)

Fenwick owes me Φ120 from the Lindhurst job split and he knows he does. If he acts like he doesn't, Demi was there, she saw the handshake. I'm not saying chase him for it. I'm saying you're allowed to.
There's Φ55 in the account under the handle threadbare_echo. I don't know if that account survives me, I don't know how Signal handles this, but if someone can get to it that money is real.

---

THINGS I WANT TO SAY

Demi: You were the first person who treated me like I was already competent instead of almost competent and I don't think you know what that did for me. I've been trying to do that for other people. I don't know if I'm doing it right. You'd tell me if I wasn't. That's why I trust you.

Tomás: Stop taking the worst positions on extraction because you think you're the most expendable. You're not more expendable than anyone else. You just keep volunteering for it and everyone lets you because it's convenient for them and I hate it. I'm putting this in a will so you have to think about it.

Lena: I'm sorry about what I said after the Caldwell Street job. I was scared and I took it out on you and that was wrong and I should have said so sooner. I hope you're somewhere good. I hope you got out of C-tier. I think you had what it takes, I just never said it.

Rocha: You're funnier than you think you are but you're less scary than you think you are and you should stop trying to be scary. It's a lot of energy.

---

THE REGRET

I want to write this down even if no one reads it.

When I was seventeen I saw someone getting beaten outside the Shelf 6 transit hub by two Arcturus guys and I had a clear angle and the right gear and I walked past. I kept walking. I told myself it wasn't my fight and it wasn't my problem and I couldn't afford the heat. Maybe all of that was true. I still walked past. I found out later the person was okay, which I used to make myself feel better, but it doesn't actually change what I did.

I've tried to be different since then. I think sometimes I am. But I wanted to write it down somewhere because it's true and it happened and I don't want to be someone who just never mentions the bad things they did.

That's the regret.

---

THE SPECIFIC REQUEST

There is a box under the floor panel in the locker, behind the boots, taped to the underside of the shelf. It's a metal box. Inside is a glass marble, blue and white, and a folded piece of paper with an address on it. The marble belongs to a kid named Piotr who lives at that address on Shelf 11. His sister gave it to me to hold during a job I did for their family fourteen months ago and said she'd come back for it and she didn't come back. I don't know why. I don't know if Piotr is still there. But if someone could try to return the marble to him I would really appreciate it. Just knock on the door and say it's from Nadia if that helps, that was her name, Nadia.

You don't have to do this one. I know it's a lot to ask. But I've been carrying it for fourteen months and I'd like it to get where it was going.

---

That's everything I think. I tried to be thorough. If I missed something use your judgment, I trust the people reading this.

Okay. Going now.
